items.statement: Among overweight dogs with osteoarthritis in first-opinion practice, the nurse-led weight clinic will improve owner-reported mobility at six months by at least 4 points more than usual vet-led advice.
items.rationale: The board's decision turns on this; the referral trial suggests an effect of this size; the 4-point threshold is what owners consider meaningful (claim c2).
items.risks: Expectation bias, attrition and practice differences.

items.statement: Dogs in the clinic will lose at least 5 percentage points more body weight at six months than dogs receiving usual advice.
items.rationale: Weight is objective and supports the mobility result.
items.risks: Weight loss without mobility change would not justify roll-out on its own.

items.statement: Blinded lameness scores will show a smaller difference than owner-reported mobility.
items.rationale: Owners report improvement from expectation (claim c3).
items.risks: Video lameness scoring is less sensitive to small changes.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected as the primary comparison.
